questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence . A) Which means that in the years ahead, one out of every five workers deployed globally could be an Indian. B) The world is indeed looking up to the Indian economy as a ‘bright star’, as the Finance Minister noted in the Budget speech on February 1. C) In 2020, India accounted for 20.6% of the worldwide population of 15 to 29 year olds. D) No doubt, the rest of the world foresees a fortune in India’s young population. E) But are our policymakers doing enough to realise the possibilities that are unfolding?
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.

A) Which means that in the years ahead, one out of every five workers deployed globally could be an Indian.

B) The world is indeed looking up to the Indian economy as a ‘bright star’, as the Finance Minister noted in the Budget speech on February 1.

C) In 2020, India accounted for 20.6% of the worldwide population of 15 to 29 year olds.

D) No doubt, the rest of the world foresees a fortune in India’s young population.

E) But are our policymakers doing enough to realise the possibilities that are unfolding?
questions.solution: B: It sets the context by referencing an authoritative figure (the Finance Minister) and mentioning a significant event (Budget speech on February 1).

questions.question: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Cuba is known as the sugar bowl of the world. It is part of the Caribbean _____________. This country _______________ a lot of sugar in the decade of 1960s.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Cuba is known as the sugar bowl of the world. It is part of the Caribbean _____________. This country _______________ a lot of sugar in the decade of 1960s.
questions.solution: 'Region' is the correct word as it means "a large geographic area," which fits the context of 'Caribbean.' While 'area' refers to a general location, it is less specific in this context. 'Stretch' implies "a span," but it is not commonly used in a geographical sense like this. 'Sector' refers to a "division" or "segment," which is not appropriate here.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Tom will _________ the document to the office tomorrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Tom will _________ the document to the office tomorrow.
questions.solution: 'Mail' will be used because it means to send something, especially through post or any other medium. In the sentence, "Tom will _________ the document to the office tomorrow," it implies sending the document, making 'mail' the correct choice. Whereas: 'Meal' means food, which doesn't fit the context. 'Male' means a man, which is irrelevant here. 'Mall' refers to a shopping complex, which doesn't make sense in this context.

questions.question: Improve the bold part in each of the following sentences, if needed. My mother is one of the few people to whom I look up to.
questions.questionHtml:
Improve the bold part in each of the following sentences, if needed.

My mother is one of the few people to whom I look up to.

options.html: I look up to
that I look up
to who I look up

options.text: to which I look up to
options.html: to which I look up to

questions.solution: A) 'to whom I look up to' will be replaced with 'I look up to' or 'that I look up to' because 'look up to' is a Phrasal Verb which means 'to praise/respect' Doing'. Hence the use of 'to whom' is unnecessary. 'That' can be used instead of 'whom' because 'that' is used as a Relative Pronoun after 'the few'/'the little'; like -

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. People whom are (A) / concerned can avoid products (B) / that contain triclosan by (C) / reading the labels. (D)
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

People whom are (A) / concerned can avoid products (B) / that contain triclosan by (C) / reading the labels. (D)

options.html: concerned can avoid products
that contain triclosan by

questions.solution: 'who' will be used instead of 'whom' because here the Relative Pronoun is used as the Subject (as the Subject of the verb 'are'), hence the Nominative Case 'who' will be used, not the Objective Case 'whom'; Like— People who are interested can join the club.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph a) Worse, learning levels decreased moving from the third to the tenth grade b) The NAS 2021 survey assessed over 3.4 million students across grades 3, 5, 8, and 10, finding that c) The National Achievement Survey (NAS) 2021, a large-scale national survey conducted every three years by the National Council of Education Research and Training (NCERT), assesses the level of children’s learning d) The average score across all grades and subjects were lower in 2021 than they were in 2017
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph

a) Worse, learning levels decreased moving from the third to the tenth grade

b) The NAS 2021 survey assessed over 3.4 million students across grades 3, 5, 8, and 10, finding that

c) The National Achievement Survey (NAS) 2021, a large-scale national survey conducted every three years by the National Council of Education Research and Training (NCERT), assesses the level of children’s learning

d) The average score across all grades and subjects were lower in 2021 than they were in 2017

options.html: d, b, a, c
d, a, b, c
c, a, d, b
c, b, d, a

questions.solution: Option A starts with d, which doesn't introduce the reader to NAS or the purpose of the survey, so A can be eliminated.
